usage: "Shukran" is the most universal way to say "thank you" in Egypt, suitable for any situation, formal or casual, regardless of gender. For more warmth or to sound more local, Egyptians often use "mitshakkir" (I am thankful) or "teslam" (may you be safe).

variants.label: I am thankful (male speaker)
variants.note: Used by a male speaker to express personal gratitude.

variants.label: I am thankful (female speaker)
variants.note: Used by a female speaker to express personal gratitude.

variants.label: casual/warm (to a man)
variants.note: A very common, warm way to thank a man for a favor or service, literally meaning 'may you be safe'.

variants.label: casual/warm (to a woman)
variants.note: A very common, warm way to thank a woman for a favor or service.

variants.label: emphatic
variants.note: Used when you want to emphasize your gratitude for something significant.

examples.english: A thousand thanks for your help.
